purpose: Extends PHASE-688's single-frame real measurement (ghibli_01_v1_cc001_subject_bbox.json) to 3 additional, already-identified real candidates from the same source (GHIBLI_01), using the exact same real toolchain and direct-visual-measurement discipline -- a minimal REPRODUCIBILITY PILOT across varied frame content, not a bulk/automated extraction and not an expansion into camera_path/motion_vectors/edit_rhythm/scene_remap or additional sources.
toolchain: identical to PHASE-688: Python 3.13.12 + imageio 2.37.3, plugin='FFMPEG' (imageio_ffmpeg bundled ffmpeg), against imports/source_videos/active/ghibli/GHIBLI_01.mp4, fps=24.0 (per the source plan's own extraction_notes)

measurements.frame_content_matches_declared_value: the subject (Kiki) appears as a small, distant figure against a wide aerial townscape -- consistent with a camera that has begun to push in from an even wider prior framing; matches the declared camera_motion:'push_in' judgment

subject_bounding_box_measurement.subject: the single visible character (small figure, arms outstretched, red bow visible)

measurements.frame_content_matches_declared_value: TWO characters visible: a boy reaching for a bundle at screen-left, and Kiki holding the bundle positioned in the right third of frame -- matches blocking:'pair_exchange' and subject_position:'right_third' (referring to Kiki) precisely
measurements.two_subject_disclosure: this frame genuinely contains two distinct characters (matching its own declared blocking:'pair_exchange'); per the plan's own subject_position:'right_third' label (which names Kiki, not the boy, as the positionally-referenced subject), this measurement covers ONLY Kiki (the right-third subject) for consistency with the single-subject methodology used in PHASE-688 and this pilot's other two measurements. measurements.frame_content_matches_declared_value: an extreme close-up, subject genuinely hard to identify unambiguously (a dark rounded shape resembling Kiki's witch hat, seen from a high angle, with a wicker basket weave in the foreground partially framing/occluding it on both sides, plus a bare foot visible at bottom) -- this frame's own difficulty directly confirms the source plan's own honest overlay_obscures_subject:true disclosure for this candidate; this pilot did not find it any easier to resolve than the original plan did

subject_bounding_box_measurement.subject: the dominant dark rounded mass in the upper-left/center of frame (most likely the witch hat), NOT a fully confident identification
subject_bounding_box_measurement.y_min_note: the mass is cut off by the frame's own top edge (zero delta), same cut-off pattern observed at bottom edges elsewhere in this pilot

cross_frame_reproducibility_summary.delta_pattern: small, non-zero, non-constant deltas on genuinely-uncertain edges; exact zero deltas ONLY where the subject is unambiguously cut off by the frame's own border (observed 3 times: PHASE-688's y_max, this pilot's cc_004 y_max, this pilot's cc_010 y_min) -- this zero-only-at-hard-boundaries pattern is itself evidence of genuine measurement (a formula would not know to produce exactly zero only at real frame edges), consistent across all 4 independent measurements now on record
cross_frame_reproducibility_summary.no_fabrication_signature_found: none of the 4 measurements show the PHASE-687-identified fabrication signature (constant delta, e.g. exactly +0.0001, or identical confidence value across records) -- each frame's deltas differ from the others'
